title: presubmit: adaptive scheduling and dependency-surface shrinker to speed CI feedback
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: our presubmit runs have grown noisy and slow; many PRs re-run large test suites even when changes only affect docs or a single package. This PR introduces an adaptive presubmit scheduler that selects a minimal test profile based on changed paths and historical test runtime signals, plus a dependency-surface shrinker that prunes development-only transitive deps from the frontend build graph to reduce install times. The change set touches GH workflows, a small custom action (presubmit-scheduler), a lightweight Go service used in CI to compute test selection, helper scripts for path classification, and a handful of lockfile updates. Key goals: 1) reduce median presubmit wall-clock time, 2) avoid unnecessary e2e / heavy integration runs for doc/infra-only PRs, 3) shrink CI install latency by trimming developer-only transitive deps detected in our monorepo. Compatibility and safety: scheduler defaults to conservative full-run on unknown paths and has a dry-run mode; a compact whitelist ensures that critical integrations are still run for sensitive directories. Linear/Jira refs are included in linked_linear/linked_jira. Checklist: - [x] presubmit action and workflow changes - [x] path-classifier script and test-suite map - [x] shrinker script and lockfile bumps - [x] docs for maintainers and ops - [x] staged rollout (dry-run then opt-in) Rollout plan: enable dry-run for 48h, compare selected test coverage vs historical flakiness, flip to enforce-by-default after validation. Monitoring: added ci/metrics to measure selection recall and latency impact; alerts if selection misses >2% of failures compared to baseline.
commits: 3 commits: 1) Add presubmit scheduler action and initial Go implementation (tools/presubmit-scheduler/*) — core scheduler, path heuristics, unit tests. 2) Integrate scheduler into .github/workflows/presubmit.yml, add dry-run and opt-in flags, update runner templates and cache layering notes. 3) Add dependency-surface shrinker script and lockfile bumps (package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml), docs and upgrade notes.
